_comment: The lexicon (landing page §01 Learn). Order is pedagogical: what you protect, who knows what, acting unnamed, proving yourself, believing others. Each card links to the article whose primary concept (concepts[0] in frontmatter) matches its id — resolved at build time, never hand-wired.

concepts.definition: Keeping what's yours from being taken — your accounts, your device, your money. Locks, keys, and who can get in.
concepts.distinction: Not the same as privacy: a service can be perfectly secure and still watch everything you do.

concepts.definition: Deciding who gets to know what about you. The bathroom door, the sealed envelope — ordinary dignity, not secrecy.
concepts.distinction: Not the same as hiding: you don't need to be doing anything wrong to want a door.

concepts.definition: Acting without your name attached — reading, browsing, or speaking without being identified.
concepts.distinction: Not the same as privacy: it's one tool privacy sometimes uses, and the wrong tool against fraud.

concepts.definition: Being able to prove you are exactly who you say you are — no more, no less, on your terms.
concepts.distinction: Not the same as surveillance: being known shouldn't mean being watched.

concepts.definition: Confidence that whoever is on the other end is who they claim to be — built on proof, not vibes.
concepts.distinction: Not the same as familiarity: a voice that sounds like your daughter isn't proof it's your daughter.
